Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to KPIT Technologies Q2 FY27
Earnings Conference Call hosted by Dolat Capital. As a reminder, all
participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should
you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by
pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note this conference
is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Rahul Jain. Thank
you and over to you, sir.
Rahul Jain: Thank you, Nazneen. Good evening, everyone. On behalf of Dolat Capital, I
would like to thank KPIT Technologies for giving us the opportunity to host
this earnings call. And now I would like to hand the conference over to Mr.
Sunil Phansalkar, who is Vice President, CF&G and Head of IR at KPIT to do
the management introductions. Over to you, Sunil.
Sunil Phansalkar: Thank you, Rahul. A warm welcome to all on the KPIT Q2 FY27 Post Earnings
Conference Call. I would like to take this opportunity to wish all of you in
advance a very happy Diwali and a prosperous New Year. On the call today,
we have Mr. Kishor Patil, Co-founder, CEO and MD; Mr. Sachin Tikekar,
President and Joint MD; Anup Sable, Board Member and COO; Chinmay Pandit,
Board Member and Head Americas; Priyamvada Hardikar CFO and yours truly
from IR.
So, as we do always, we will have the opening remarks by Mr. Kishor Patil on
the performance of the quarter and the way we look at the year ahead and
then we will have it open for questions. So, once again, a very warm welcome
to you all and I will hand this over to Mr. Kishor Patil.
Kishor Patil: Good evening and thank you for joining the call. Welcome to quarter 2
Earnings call. Sometime back, we had given how KPIT growth will pan out and
specifically in terms of how Q2 will look like. And we are happy that we are
in line with our expectations and we can see some of the early results of the
strategy we have put in place.
So in order to really understand this, let's go into the details. So, overall
growth has been 6.5% year-on-year and 1%, in terms of quarter-on-quarter,
in rupee terms. We were expecting more flattish in CC terms, which came at
0.5% quarter-on-quarter and 0.2% year-on-year. So, looking at this, if we go
one level below, off highway and Commercial has grown 27% year-on-year
and 17.6% quarter-on-quarter.
So as we had mentioned, this is one of the growth drivers for now and for the
future that we are looking at. The passenger car, if you really look at it, we
are down by about 8% year-on-year and 4% sequentially. I would like to
mention here that while passenger car growth looks like this, if we take out

our two top accounts, where we had an impact due to a sharp decline we
had due to cancellation of their programs or cutting off their expense was
13% of the total revenue.
So what this means is we have been in a position to make up that drop due
to our growth in off-highway and Commercial vehicles and also from the
Products . So, this is how we have been in a position to make up. The pipeline
is healthy. We have got reasonable wins and now 89% of the wins have come
from target accounts. The pipeline is an active pipeline and we see that while
it is taking some time for realization, it is an active pipeline and we feel much
more comfortable with some of the opportunities on hand. I would like to
come back to the Products. The Products revenue which we have talked about
in the past and we will talk more about this later in the year, maybe early
next year, in more detail what we intend to do.
But this we have a 5% growth quarter-on-quarter during the quarter and 25%
year-on-year. So overall services revenue has been flattish, but Products have
grown 5% quarter-on-quarter and 25% year-on-year. In terms of profitability,
our EBITDA has grown from 17.2% to 17.8%, this is 60 basis point, largely it is
because of the business mix as the products contributions are higher as
compared to the services part and solutions part.
And we have continued to make investments in terms of technology. Even
during this quarter, our investments into R&D has gone up by a couple of
million dollars. So, our Net cash is about INR 6.2 billion. It has come down a
bit, basically for two, three reasons. One is the there was a dividend payment
of INR 1.4 billion.
There was an acquisition payment of Cymotive in the sense the initial
payment of Cymotive about a billion. And the DSO has increased from 51 days
to 53 days. The wins I talked have been mainly in terms of Autonomy,
Connected and IDART. In terms of AI, if you really look at, we continue to
make good strides in that.
We believe that this will be for now and in medium term a very significant
differentiator. The Beacon product has been very well received. And as most
of all our, almost all our products, the Beacon is the basis for that, while we
also will take Beacon to the market in due course.
In services and solutions, of course, on all our deliveries, many of our
deliveries, we have started using this. There are more than 9,000 users of the
AI platform, our overall AI product. We have more than 5 million transactions,
if I would say, which have happened during the quarter. 12,000 engineering
agents have been built.

it will take time to have a meaningful impact. But this is what we have already
initiated. We do believe that we are really excited, on the AI-native deliveries,
AI products which we have.
The overall products chain, the way we have done from the architecture to
after-sales, the solutions we are building around the products and
adjacencies. So while our performance is, as I said, in line but muted to some
extent, we remain confident about the midterm growth. Excited about the
opportunity we have in front of us. Thank you.
Sunil Phansalkar: We can open it for questions now.
Moderator: Thank you very much. The first question is from the line of Rishabh Rathi from
Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.
Rishabh Rathi: Hi, good evening and thank you for the opportunity. My question is around the
geography-wise sales and we had talked about the 2 major customers winding
down. If I can just see Europe, actually we have seen a sequential decline but
Asia has picked up in 2Q versus 1Q. So if you could just give some color
whether going forward we can see more sequential decline and is there some
positive development in Asia next of the customer decline?
Sachin Tikekar: Hi, Rishabh, this is Sachin Tikekar. So the 2 clients where we have seen a
sharp decline, one happens to be in Japan which is part of JKC and the other
one is in Europe. And it's primarily because of these two clients you see
degrowth in the 2 respective geographies. There is growth in Americas as you
can see in the US quarter-on-quarter, year-on-year. SIMA, which we split
from Asia. So Asia has 2 parts, one is JKC, Japan, Korea, China.
The other part is, Southeast Asia, India, Middle East. And that's where we
again see growth, primarily driven by, fairly, well-rounded growth, primarily
driven by India in, in SIMA. So, the way to look at, the split is, the issue is
actually with these 2 OEMs where the revenue has gone down by more than
13%.
And we do believe that in the next couple of quarters that both these clients
will bottom out. And till that time, there is an opportunity for us to bring
broad-based, more resilient growth and what we mean by that is the growth
will happen. A: In existing clients of passenger cars, in new clients that we
have picked up in passenger cars. B: More clients in off-highway.
So one is, last quarter we announced one software-defined machine kind of
an engagement with one OEM. Now there are 2 consulting engagements in
SDM, 2 additional ones. And usually consulting one, all going well, they lead
to actual SDM program. So positive development on off-highway as well.

Priya Hardikar: There are a couple of reasons I think we've mentioned in our investor deck.
There have been cash outflows on account of dividend, some acquisition
payment that we did for Cymotive. And others, as you can see, our DSOs have
gone up by a couple of days. That also has impacted the working capital cycle.
Ravi: Ma’am, only the DSO would impact the OCF. The other factor that you
mentioned will actually not be in the operating cash flow, right?
Priya Hardikar: Yes. So but the fundamental reason is the working capital cycle that has gone
up because of, increase in DSOs.
Ravi: All right. Okay, thank you. I'll get back into it.
Rahul Jain: Thank you.
Moderator: Thank you. Next question is from the line of Karan from PhillipCapital India.
Please go ahead.
Karan: Yes, thanks for the opportunity. So just wanted to check in terms of the
growth outlook for next few quarters, given that the headwinds will continue
in 2 of our largest clients, but you are also positive on the pipeline. So how
should we think about the growth from next few quarters perspective?
Kishor Patil: So, I think we have mentioned last time that H2 will be better than H1. I think
we will maintain that. And we also feel confident that we'll make up for the
drop from these clients with the broad-based growth strategy which we have.
So these are the 2 things I can say. So there will be a growth, and both things
which we have mentioned earlier, I would like to reiterate.
Karan: Okay. So last time, sir, you had mentioned that you should see some rebound
from Q4 onwards. So is that outlook intact?
Kishor Patil: So we expect growth, and we will not be in a position to put any numbers
now, but we expect growth in that quarter.
Karan: Got it. Second question is on the CV. So CV segment has been growing quite
strongly for us for last 4 to 5 quarters. Is the growth broad-based in this
segment or it's concentrated in 1 or 2 large accounts? And also is the growth
sustainable over the medium term within this?
Sachin Tikekar: Yes, so CV, when we look at CV we look at it in 2 verticals, one is off-highway,
mostly construction, mining. And second is trucks. So so off-highway is
somewhat new to us, so we already have 3 clients and we're adding 2 more.
So right now, of course, it's concentrated at the beginning on the back of 3
clients, but it's becoming more broad-based.
